Wireless Call Receiver is an accessibility tool for blind and visually impaired users. While enabled, it can access supported incoming call notifications and the visible text, labels, view identifiers, and window structure of supported call interfaces. It can observe configured headset or volume key events and perform a targeted click or tap on an Answer or End Call control. If you enable Auto-Answer, it may perform the answer action automatically after a detected incoming call.\n\nThis processing occurs on your device. The app does not collect, sell, share, or transmit this data, and it does not contain Internet permission. You can decline now and enable the service later.

Notification Access lets Wireless Call Receiver inspect notification package names, call categories, action labels, and temporary action tokens from supported phone and internet-calling apps so it can detect an incoming call and invoke the Answer or End Call action. It does not read or store message bodies, and no notification data is transmitted or shared. Temporary call action information is kept only in memory while needed.\n\nYou can decline now and enable this access later.
You may finish setup after declining any item. Features that need missing access will remain unavailable until you grant it later.

Wireless Call Receiver is an accessibility tool designed primarily for blind and visually impaired users. It helps users answer or end supported cellular and internet calls with configured Bluetooth hardware controls. If the user explicitly enables Auto-Answer, the app may answer a detected incoming call after the configured delay.

Depending on the access you grant, the app processes Bluetooth connection state and device name; supported call-notification package names, categories, action labels, and temporary action tokens; supported call-screen text, labels, view identifiers, and window structure; and configured hardware-key events. It does not access contacts, call history, microphone audio, camera, location, message bodies, or files.

The developer does not collect, sell, share, or transmit personal or sensitive data. The app has no Internet permission, advertising SDK, or analytics SDK. Call-related information is processed locally and temporary action tokens are retained only in memory while needed. App preferences are stored locally and may be included in Android system backup or device transfer according to your device settings. Uninstalling the app removes its local app data.

Bluetooth access detects a connected headset. Notification permission displays the foreground-service status. Answer Phone Calls enables the Telecom call-answer fallback. Accessibility and Notification Access support call detection and targeted actions for supported apps. Each request is separate; you may decline or revoke access in Android Settings, and affected features will stop working. The app is provided as-is, may not work with every device or calling app, and must not be relied on for emergency communications. No account is created. For policy questions or support, use the project support page linked from the public website.

Sensitive call information is limited to on-device processing and is not written to developer-controlled servers. Android protects the Accessibility and Notification Listener services with system binding permissions. You can delete locally stored preferences by clearing the app\'s storage or uninstalling it. Because the app creates no user account and the developer collects no user data, there is no developer-held account data to delete.

The app is not specifically directed to children under 13 and does not knowingly collect children\'s data. Material policy changes will be published on the public website with an updated effective date. Continued use after an update is subject to the revised terms.
